correctness.rationale: For every r>0 and theta, the four lifted rows follow from direct expansion. Their determinant is the Vandermonde product of nodes 1,r²,re^{iθ},re^{-iθ} times a constant. Optimizing its positive phase factor leads to 6rx²-(1+r²)x-4r=0, with one root in (-1,0) and the other beyond 1 for r≠1. This proves the global equality set and nondegenerate maxima. Symmetry and limits follow from s=r+r^{-1}. The singular boundaries have explicit non-phase-equivalent pairs. Standard-library checker independently reproduced 12,473 finite assertions, not used to infer the universal proof.

value.rationale: Four observations form a natural dimension-matched linear intensity-lifting experiment for two complex modes. With independent homoscedastic intensity errors, the sharp determinant maximizer minimizes generalized covariance volume of the unconstrained lifted estimator. The exact formula yields a usable phase-choice rule, two equality orientations, reciprocal-damping symmetry and boundaries of nonidentifiability. Its scope is intentionally not arbitrary sampling or nonlinear noise-optimal phase retrieval.
